title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX2Root Flaws as PoC Exploits Go Public
content_md: F5 on Wednesday announced patches for 22 vulnerabilities, including five critical-severity NGINX bugs that could lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Referred to as NGINX2Root, the five issues are tracked as CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, and CVE-2026-123634 (CVSS score of 9.2). CVE-2026-113425 affects NGINX instances configured as mail proxy servers and can be exploited via specially crafted mail sessions. CVE-2026-121810 can be exploited on servers that use HTTP/3 to trigger a use-after-free in the NGINX worker process. CVE-2026-123634 impacts servers configured as proxies and can be triggered if the proxied server name includes variables, and a subrequest to a location resolving that server name is received from a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive. CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 require HTTP/2 to be enabled on an affected server. Successful exploitation of the former leads to a buffer overflow, while the latter triggers a use-after-free in the worker process. The two issues were independently reported by Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, Wiz, and Xint. They explain that attackers could exploit them to run commands with the privileges of the nginx worker process and fully compromise the server. “Our testing of CVE-2026-123007 demonstrated code execution on NGINX serving ordinary static files, without a backend application or third-party modules,” Wiz explains, noting

CVE-2026-123007.evidence: SecurityWeek reports public PoC exploits and Wiz demonstrated code execution against ordinary static-file NGINX; no victim campaign is described.
